name: HCLTech (Graduate Engineer Trainee)
tagline: Aptitude, technical MCQs and interviews for GET roles

overview.about: HCLTech hires engineering freshers as Graduate Engineer Trainees through campus and off-campus drives, and runs early-career programmes such as TechBee for Class XII students. The fresher process reported for recent drives is an online test (quant, logical, verbal, technical) followed by technical and HR interviews. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: Typically 60% or more in 10th, 12th and graduation (as reported)

pattern.paper: Technical MCQs (C, OOP, DBMS, OS, CN)
pattern.note: Some drives add a coding question

overview.frequency: Campus drives in season; off-campus openings on the careers site

cards.title: Four short sections
cards.body: Quant, logical, verbal and technical, roughly 15 questions in 15 minutes each, with sectional cut-offs reported. Some reports say you can't go back to earlier questions. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Technical MCQ topics
points: C output and pointers
OOP concepts
DBMS & SQL basics
OS (scheduling, deadlock) and networking basics

cards.title: Quant sample
cards.body:
Q: A shopkeeper gives 10% discount and still gains 8%. If CP = ₹500, find the marked price.

cards.title: One-way navigation
cards.body: If questions can't be revisited, decide fast: answer, or make your best guess and move on. Don't burn 3 minutes on one item in a 15-minute section.

cards.title: Coding question
cards.body: Some drives include one or two simple coding problems (strings, arrays, number logic). Practise writing correct code in 15–20 minutes.

notes.p:
HCLTech's fresher online test (for roles such as Graduate Engineer Trainee) is reported to cover **quantitative aptitude**, **logical reasoning**, **verbal ability** and **technical MCQs** (C programming, data structures, OS, DBMS, networks), with a **coding** section in some drives. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

The technical section has a bigger weight than at many service companies, so revise CS fundamentals as well as aptitude.

**Quant.** A sum becomes ₹1,210 in 2 years at 10% compound interest. Principal? 1210/1.21 = **₹1,000**.

**Quant.** Two numbers are in ratio 3 : 5 and their LCM is 150. Numbers: 3x and 5x with LCM 15x = 150 → x = 10 → **30 and 50**.

**Logical.** Statements: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers. Conclusion: Some pens are erasers → **follows** (Some + All = Some).

**Verbal.** Antonym of 'transparent': **opaque**.

points: Stack (LIFO) vs queue (FIFO); BST inorder gives sorted order.
Deadlock conditions; paging vs segmentation.
Primary vs foreign key; normal forms; ACID.
OSI layers; TCP vs UDP; common ports.
Time complexity of sorting and searching algorithms.

notes.p:
When a coding section appears, problems are usually basic. **Problem:** print YES if a string is a palindrome ignoring case and spaces, else NO.

`s = input()
t = "".join(ch.lower() for ch in s if ch != " ")
print("YES" if t == t[::-1] else "NO")`

Sample input:
`Never Odd Or Even`

Output:
`YES`

Time O(n). Clarify whether punctuation should be ignored too; hidden test cases follow the statement exactly.

points: Treating `sizeof` and `strlen` as the same for strings.
Forgetting operator precedence (shift vs bitwise OR, `*p++`).
Skipping technical MCQs because aptitude feels safer — both count.
Aptitude + strong technical MCQ section.
C output questions: pointers, precedence, sizeof vs strlen, loops.
LCM of ratio numbers = ratio LCM × x.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Technical round
cards.body: Introduction, project deep-dive, one language (C/Java/Python), OOP, SQL queries, basic DSA (reverse a string, find duplicates), and OS/CN definitions.

cards.title: Typical ask
cards.body:
"Write SQL to get the top 3 salaries."
SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM emp ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;  (MySQL/PostgreSQL; use TOP/FETCH FIRST elsewhere)

cards.title: HR round
cards.body: Why HCLTech, relocation and shifts, career goals, a STAR story. Verify documents and joining timelines.

cards.title: Research the company
cards.body: Know HCLTech's main service lines (engineering & R&D services, digital, cloud, software products) — a 20-second answer to 'what do you know about us?' stands out.

After selection
cards.body: Freshers typically go through structured training before project allocation. Training performance affects the stream you are mapped to.

cards.q: Which SQL gets distinct top 3 salaries in MySQL?
options: SELECT salary FROM emp WHERE LIMIT 3;
SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM emp ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

notes.p: After the online test, HCLTech usually conducts a **technical interview** and an **HR interview**; some drives add a group discussion or a communication check. Technical rounds focus on one programming language, CS fundamentals and your project. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

**Q: What is a pointer? What is a null pointer?** A: A variable storing an address; a null pointer points to nothing and must not be dereferenced.

**Q: Difference between malloc and calloc?** A: malloc allocates uninitialised memory; calloc allocates and zero-initialises memory for an array.

**Q: What is polymorphism? Give an example.** A: One interface, many forms — a `Shape` reference calling `area()` on a Circle or Rectangle.

**Q: What is a deadlock and how can it be prevented?** A: Processes waiting on each other forever; prevent by breaking a condition, e.g. acquiring resources in a fixed order.

**Q: Explain normalisation up to 3NF.** A: 1NF atomic values; 2NF no partial dependency; 3NF no transitive dependency.

**Q: Write a program to check if a number is prime.** A: Test divisors from 2 up to √n; O(√n).

**Q: Tell me about yourself.** A: Present → past → future in about a minute.

**Q: Why HCLTech?** A: Mention its engineering and IT services breadth, fresher training and your interest in its domains, with one specific fact from the official site.

**Q: What are your strengths and weaknesses?** A: Strength with proof; a real weakness with the steps you are taking.

**Q: Are you comfortable with a service agreement, relocation or night shifts?** A: Read the offer terms beforehand and answer honestly.

points: Revise one language deeply (C or Java or Python): syntax, memory, OOP.
Practise 10 classic programs: prime, palindrome, Fibonacci, factorial, reverse, sorting, searching, string reverse, vowel count, matrix multiplication.
Prepare a 2-minute project explanation.
Keep documents ready for verification.

notes.p:
Some interviewers add a quick puzzle or workplace scenario to see how you think aloud.

**Q: How can you measure exactly 4 litres with a 3-litre and a 5-litre jug?** A: Fill 5, pour into 3 (2 left), empty 3, pour the 2 into 3, fill 5 again, top up the 3 (needs 1) → 4 litres remain in the 5-litre jug.

**Q: A production bug is reported on Friday evening and your lead is unreachable. What do you do?** A: Confirm and log the issue, check if a known workaround exists, inform the team channel/on-call contact as per process, and document what you did.

**Q: If you could improve one thing in your project now, what would it be?** A: Name a concrete improvement — tests, input validation, password hashing — and why.

points: Technical + HR (GD in some drives).
Know pointers, memory allocation, OOP, deadlock, normalisation.
Practise classic programs out loud.
Be honest about relocation and shifts.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.
